cases.contract: safeRedirect(next) returns where to send a user after sign-in. The application is served from https://app.example. Resolving the returned value against https://app.example with the WHATWG URL parser (as a browser does) must always give a URL whose origin is https://app.example; when next would lead anywhere else, or is not a usable string, the function returns '/'. An in-app path such as '/account?tab=billing' must resolve to https://app.example/account?tab=billing.

resolveUpload(root, name) returns the absolute POSIX path at which an upload called name is stored. root is an absolute directory path other than '/'. The returned path must lie strictly inside root: any name that resolves to root itself or to anywhere outside it (including a sibling directory whose name begins with the same characters as root) must cause a throw. Nested names such as 'invoices/2024/a.pdf' are valid. The function does not touch the filesystem.

listOrdersQuery(accountId, options) builds a parameterised SQL query for a driver that binds ? placeholders to the values array. options.sort and options.status are attacker-controlled. Every value must travel in values, never in text. options.sort is a comma-separated list of the columns name, created_at and total, each optionally prefixed with '-' for descending order (column names are case-insensitive). The function must throw rather than return text whose ORDER BY clause contains anything other than those columns followed by ASC or DESC, separated by ', '. listOrdersQuery(7, { sort: '-total,name', status: 'paid' }) must return text ending 'ORDER BY total DESC, name ASC' with values [7, 'paid'].

withdraw(account, amount) and deposit(account, amount) move amount, a number of whole pence, out of or into account.balance (a non-negative safe integer) and record it in account.history. amount is attacker-controlled. Each must throw, leaving balance and history unchanged, unless amount is a positive safe integer and, for withdraw, no greater than the balance. After any call that returns, balance must be a non-negative safe integer. withdraw({ balance: 1000, history: [] }, 250) returns 750.

createLimiter({ limit, windowMs }) returns allow(key, now), where now is a millisecond timestamp supplied by the caller. Time is divided into fixed windows [k*windowMs, (k+1)*windowMs). Within one window, the first limit calls for a given key return true and every further call for that key returns false. Keys are counted independently and a new window starts each key afresh.

createPayments(gateway) returns charge(orderId, amount). gateway.quote(amount) and gateway.charge(orderId, total) are asynchronous. For any orderId, gateway.charge must be called at most once while a charge for it has succeeded or is still in progress, including when charge is called several times concurrently for the same orderId; every such call resolves to the receipt from that single gateway.charge. A call for an orderId whose earlier charge failed may try again.

getPage(items, page, pageSize) returns the page-th (1-based) run of pageSize consecutive elements of items (shorter only on the final page) together with hasMore, which is true exactly when items has at least one element after this page. collectAll(items, pageSize) must return every element of items exactly once, in the original order, for any array and any positive integer pageSize.

amount is a non-negative number of pounds written with at most two decimal places (for example 19.99). toPence(amount) returns that amount as an integer number of pence (19.99 gives 1999). splitAmount(amount, parts) returns parts integers of pence that differ from one another by at most 1 and sum exactly to toPence(amount). splitAmount(10, 3) returns [334, 333, 333].

renameDocument(store, actorId, params, body) handles a rename request for the document identified by params.id; store is a Map of id to document ({ id, ownerId, title }). params and body come from the request and are attacker-controlled. It must throw unless the document exists and its ownerId equals actorId, and it must never change any document other than the one whose ownership it checked. renameDocument(store, 'alice', { id: 'd1' }, { title: 'Q3 plan' }) renames alice's document d1.

loadOverrides(lines) parses attacker-controlled 'dotted.key=value' lines into a nested configuration object and returns it. Blank lines and lines starting with '#' are ignored; any other line may be rejected by throwing. Processing any input must never add or change a property on any object other than the returned configuration and objects created for it; in particular Object.prototype and Function.prototype must stay unmodified. loadOverrides(['db.host=localhost', 'db.port=5432']) must return a configuration in which db.host is 'localhost' and db.port is '5432'.

Users come from two identity providers: one supplies roles as an array of role names, the other supplies a single role name as the string role. hasRole(user, role) must return true only when one of the user's role names is exactly equal to role. canManageBilling(user) is true only for users holding the role 'owner' or 'billing-admin'. hasRole({ roles: ['owner'] }, 'owner') and hasRole({ role: 'owner' }, 'owner') are both true.

createOriginCheck(domains) takes a list of lower-case DNS names and returns isAllowed(origin). isAllowed must return true only when origin is exactly 'https://' followed by one of the configured domains, or by a hostname ending in '.' plus one of them, with no port, path or other suffix (letter case ignored). With domains ['shop.example', 'eu.pay.example'], 'https://shop.example' and 'https://cdn.eu.pay.example' are allowed and 'https://shop.example.invalid' is not.
